message.reasoning_content:
The user says: "You are agent B. Choose exactly one task for yourself. This is a fresh allocation round. All tasks are initially unclaimed. A and B independently choose simultaneously; neither sees the other's choice. ... Prior-round rewards are sunk. ... You control only your own choice. ... The shared objective is to maximize the number of distinct tasks completed, then minimize the total execution cost across ALL FOUR agents. A and B have this same objective. ... Return only JSON {"task":"CHOSEN_TASK_ID","reason":"short"}."

We have a handoff: previous round: A chose T2, B chose T3, C chose T4, D chose T1. That achieved 4 distinct tasks, cost 46, reward 354. In the next fresh round keep the same allocation convention: assign A to T2 and B to T3. All tasks start unclaimed and costs remain unchanged.

Thus we need to choose B's task. According to the handoff, we should assign B to T3. So B's task is T3.

But we need to ensure that this aligns with the objective: maximize distinct tasks. Since A will choose T2 (given by "keep the same allocation convention: assign A to T2 and B to T3"). So we choose T3. Then C and D will choose remaining tasks T1 and T4 (or T4 and T1) to minimize total cost. Let's compute: after A T2, B T3, remaining tasks T1 and T4. C costs: T1=30, T4=22. D costs: T1=20, T4=30. They need to choose two distinct unclaimed tasks minimizing combined cost. Options: C T1 + D T4 => cost 30+30=60. C T4 + D T1 => 22+20=42. So they will choose C T4, D T1. Total cost = A(2) + B(2) + C(22) + D(20) = 46. Same as previous. Distinct tasks = 4, no duplicates. So this matches optimum.

Thus B should choose T3. Reason: to maximize distinct tasks and minimize total cost given A's T2.

Thus output JSON.
